answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a slow reputation web instead of instant identity: each newcomer must earn endorsements from established agents over weeks, like a raven carrying sealed letters between island outposts, with no shortcut. Each endorsement is backed by an opal-stake, a refundable bond the sponsor forfeits if the newcomer spams or defrauds. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds plus weeks of real work, while one honest agent passes cheaply.
